label: San Antonio

county_election_office.name: Bexar County Elections Department, 1103 S. Frio St., Suite 100, San Antonio 78207

zip_caveats: ZIPs do not map to Bexar County ballots. For your exact ballot, look yourself up at Bexar County Elections (elections.bexar.gov: "Individual Sample Ballot" by address or by voter) or call 210-335-VOTE. Inside San Antonio these lines all split ZIP codes: four congressional districts (CD-20, 21, 23 and 35; under the 2025 map CD-28 no longer reaches Bexar County, so it is not on any San Antonio ballot); state Senate Districts 19, 21 and 26; ten Texas House districts (HD-116 to 125; HD-120 and HD-123 have one candidate each); county commissioner precincts (only Precincts 2 and 4 vote this year, so Precinct 1 and 3 voters see no commissioner race); justice of the peace precincts (only Precincts 1, 3 and 4 have races; there is no Precinct 2 race and no constable race anywhere in Bexar County this year); and Edwards Aquifer Authority District 1. School districts cross ZIPs too. San Antonio ISD and Northside ISD have tax and bond props; South San Antonio ISD and East Central ISD have tax rate props; Edgewood ISD (West Side) has four trustee races; Somerset ISD (far southwest) has two; Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD and Comal ISD reach only small edges of the San Antonio area. North East ISD, Harlandale, Southwest, Southside, Judson, Alamo Heights and the military base school districts have nothing on this ballot. City of San Antonio Prop A is only for people who live inside city limits. A San Antonio mailing address in unincorporated Bexar County (common in 78253, 78254, 78255, 78260 and 78261) does not count, and the separate cities inside or next to San Antonio do not vote on it: for example Alamo Heights and Terrell Hills (78209), Olmos Park (78212), Castle Hills (78213), Balcones Heights (78201), Leon Valley (78238 and 78240), Shavano Park (78231), Hollywood Park and Hill Country Village (78232), Windcrest (78239), Kirby (78219), Converse (78109 and part of 78244) and Live Oak (78148 and 78233). Some of those cities (Converse, Hollywood Park, Live Oak, Windcrest) have their own races or props, including a Converse vote on leaving VIA, that this guide does not cover. A small part of San Antonio lies in Comal and Medina counties; those residents get a different county ballot, which this guide does not cover, though they still vote on Prop A. A few voters in new developer districts (special improvement districts, a municipal management district and Bexar County MUD No. 1) also get extra props. Everything countywide (district attorney, county judge, clerks, every district court, county court at law and probate court, the appraisal district board, and the 4th and 15th Courts of Appeals) is on every Bexar County ballot. The ZIP list here is a convenience list of ZIPs that are mostly inside the city, not an official crosswalk.
notes: Bexar County uses vote centers: any registered Bexar County voter can vote at any Bexar County polling place, early or on Election Day. Early voting runs Mon Oct 19 to Fri Oct 30. Most sites: Oct 19 to 23, 8 AM to 6 PM; Sat Oct 24, 7 AM to 7 PM; Sun Oct 25, noon to 6 PM; Oct 26 to 30, 7 AM to 7 PM. The two branch sites (Bexar County Justice Center and Valley Ranch Community Center) are open weekdays 8 AM to 6 PM only. Election Day, Tue Nov 3, is 7 AM to 7 PM. Mail ballot applications must be received by Fri Oct 23. Bring your printed or handwritten notes into the booth (take them with you when you leave). Phones cannot be used inside the voting room. Texas has no straight-ticket voting, so you mark every race one by one; the Bexar ballot is long, mostly judges, and many races have only one name. Skipping a race is fine. On the ballot, each proposition says "For" or "Against": For means yes, Against means no. There is no San Antonio mayor or city council race this year; Prop A is the only City of San Antonio item.
